target_customer: Companies with mobile and field workforces in Hong Kong and Asia, sold through telecom carriers; planned expansion to the US and Europe
problem: Enterprises needed secure messaging and workflow for employees working on mobile devices, including shift management and field-to-HQ photo reporting.
business_model: Enterprise subscription, white-label deployments, partly resold by telecom carriers
product_category: Enterprise mobile messaging and workforce communication

founders.name: Roy Law
founders.background_notes: Team had worked together since 2010 per TechCrunch.

founders.name: Jon Yip
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page; role and background not given.

competitors.name: Slack
competitors.what: Team messaging app; the YC tagline calls TeamNote 'Slack for mobile workforces' and TechCrunch cites Slack-style team apps as the free-trial, word-of-mouth model TeamNote planned to copy

technical_complexity.rationale: Secure messaging apps with expiring messages, shifts and photo reporting are standard mobile and backend work; the team had years of enterprise app experience.

defensibility.rationale: Carrier distribution in Hong Kong and enterprise deployments (private cloud, on-premises white label) added some stickiness, but messaging features were copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Sources do not show a takeover. Slack grew into the dominant team messaging product; no evidence it bought or targeted TeamNote. Wikipedia describes TeamNote as a white-label product not listed in app stores.

market_need_then: In March 2015 TechCrunch reported customers from teams of ten up to large organizations, including Cheung Kong's property management arm and Hong Kong and Macau government workers, and telecom carriers reselling the app, showing local enterprise demand.

branding.domain_note: Uses teamnoteapp.com, not the exact teamnote.com; history not found.

identity.logo: Logo shown on the YC page; not described

brand_strength.rationale: A descriptive, generic name for a crowded category and little brand coverage; awards (Hong Kong ICT 2015) were for the product.

outcome_analysis: TeamNote was spun out of the Hong Kong app developer AppTask, joined YC in Winter 2015 with a $120K investment and won Hong Kong ICT awards in 2015. Wikipedia reports a later angel round of roughly US$1M but no outcome after 2015; the YC directory still lists it Active with 11 people, yet there is no public evidence of growth, a US launch or further funding. The record is therefore thin and no success or failure factors are asserted.
notes: Wikipedia says TeamNote later raised roughly US$1M in an angel round with no date; that is a single source so it is not recorded as a round. CB Insights lists Taiwan Startup Stadium as an investor with no amount. TechCrunch gave no funding amount. The company site teamnoteapp.com returned empty content when fetched, so current activity is unconfirmed. Wikipedia says development began in 2012 and the company became independent in July 2013; YC lists 2014 as the founding year. Web Archive skipped.
